questions.stem: Why are carboxylic acids described as weak acids?

options.text: They only partially dissociate in water
They do not react with metals
They have a very low concentration

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids are weak acids because they only partially dissociate in water. The equilibrium lies to the left, so most molecules remain undissociated: CH3COOH <=> CH3COO- + H+. This means they have a higher pH than a strong acid of the same concentration.

questions.stem: What are the products when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
questions.explanation: When ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate, three products form: sodium ethanoate (the salt), water, and carbon dioxide gas. The CO2 causes observable fizzing. The equation is: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 -> 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2.
